subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current code and tests make persisted session exec defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because old session state can shadow later operator policy changes.

options.title: Make config the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent policy, with migration or doctor/reset coverage for existing sessions.

options.title: Keep persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset or repair sessions to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent policy, with migration or doctor/reset coverage for existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct history for introducing and testing `/exec` session overrides points to this owner path.
